I have farmed this land for 40 years, so I know what works here in Quzhou. My 9 mu is not big, but with just two of us in the household, I manage it myself with some hired help at wheat harvest and cotton picking.

I divide my land this way: 6 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, and 3 mu in cotton. The wheat-maize double crop is my main income — the ground stays busy all year. Cotton I keep because the price has been decent and my wife handles the picking.

**Winter wheat (6 mu):** I will plant Jimai 22, an improved variety — my neighbors got 500 kg last year with it. I sow around October 8, base fertilizer is diammonium phosphate 25 kg plus urea 10 kg per mu before ploughing. Topdress 15 kg urea per mu at jointing stage in March. That gives me about 20 kg N, 11 kg P₂O₅, and 6 kg K₂O per mu (I add a bit of compound fertilizer). I irrigate 3 times — before winter, jointing, and grain filling. Two pesticide sprays: one for aphids/powdery mildew at booting, one for wheat midge if I see them. Plough before sowing to break up the maize stubble. I expect 500 kg/mu.

**Summer maize (6 mu):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I plant Zhengdan 958, a hybrid — reliable here. No-tillage direct seeding into wheat stubble saves time and moisture. Base fertilizer 40 kg compound (15-15-15) per mu at sowing, then topdress 20 kg urea at big trumpet stage. That works out to 24 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. I irrigate twice if the rain is poor — at seedling and tasseling. One pesticide spray for corn borer. Expect 550 kg/mu.

**Cotton (3 mu):** Bt cotton hybrid seed, I buy from the same dealer every year. I plough deep in March, apply 30 kg compound fertilizer and 15 kg urea as base, then topdress 15 kg urea at flowering and 10 kg at boll-setting. Total about 22 kg N, 7 kg P, 10 kg K per mu — cotton likes potassium. Irrigate 3 times from well. Pesticide 4 times — aphids early, then bollworm watching even with Bt, plus mite control in summer. Expect 280 kg/mu seed cotton.

I keep fertilizer rates slightly above what the extension station suggests. A bad harvest takes years to recover from; a bag of extra urea is 130 yuan I can afford.
